regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unimpeachable until you notice the FY estimate has been revised down to 7.1% YoY and core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%. The PMI composite at 56.5 and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY are genuine — capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity confirms investment is real, not budgeted. The inversion: services credit surging at 28.3% YoY is doing the heavy lifting that goods production cannot sustain alone; if services credit tightens under macro-prudential pressure, the growth quality degrades faster than the headline suggests.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 6.09% YoY has now risen three consecutive months, but the decomposition is more alarming than the headline: food at 8.94% YoY is supply-driven and sticky, fuel at 22.93% YoY is at the 95th percentile of the decade, and core CPI has accelerated to 4.5% YoY — meaning this is no longer a food-and-fuel story. WPI at 9.92% YoY signals producer prices are feeding through. The RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY is already below the current print; the pause is increasingly a fiction the data is refusing to support.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.54% YoY against deposit growth of 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps gap widening for three consecutive months — has pushed the CD ratio to 82%, its highest since FY14. Services credit at 28.3% YoY is the accelerant; NBFC credit growth at 15.4% YoY is already decelerating as wholesale funding costs bite. The historical precedent is precise: the last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate pause, the RBI followed with macro-prudential tightening on risk weights within two quarters. The incentive for banks to keep growing credit for fee income is intact; the deposit base to fund it is not.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being compressed in real time: CPI at 6.09% YoY puts the real repo rate at -84 bps and falling. The RBI's inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY is now a lagging fiction. A pause made sense when core CPI was 3.4%; at 4.5% YoY and rising, the pause is an implicit easing. The second-order effect: negative real rates with a 82% CD ratio and FII outflows of ₹4,516 cr / month is the classic setup for INR pressure — the RBI will face a choice between defending the currency and defending growth, and it cannot do both.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — both rising — confirm the investment upcycle is real and broadening. The 75% threshold that historically triggers private capex acceleration has been crossed; iron ore at $161.91/t, up sharply from $90.86/t, signals commodity markets are pricing the same conclusion. The contradiction: core sector growth at 4.8% YoY is slipping even as capital goods surge, suggesting the investment is concentrated in manufacturing and industry rather than infrastructure. Credit to industry at 19.5% YoY supports this — but if the CD ratio forces a credit tightening, the capex cycle's funding base narrows precisely when it should be widening.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month — 90th percentile of the decade — is the strongest consumption signal in the data set, but the composition matters. Passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY suggest both urban and rural demand are firing simultaneously, which is unusual and worth interrogating. Two-wheeler sales are the rural proxy; their surge after three weak months (7.9% YoY prior) may reflect a base effect rather than a structural revival. The GST jump from ₹1,88,125 cr / month to ₹2,31,290 cr / month in one month is too large to be pure demand — advance filings and formalization effects are the more parsimonious explanation.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months (13.8→17.1→19.4→19.54% credit; 10.8→17.8→16.86% deposits). CD ratio now at 82% credit ÷ deposits, up from 81% prior month. Services credit surging at 28.3% YoY (21.4→22.9→24.3→28.3% over three months) while agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY. NBFC credit growth at 15.4% YoY, down from 15.8% — wholesale funding stress evident.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and retail deposit franchises (HDFC Bank, Kotak, Axis) — they will poach deposits from weaker peers. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity stress will force asset sales or margin compression. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 6-8 weeks if credit-deposit gap widens further. Reduce exposure to smaller PSU banks dependent on bulk deposits.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 82% is at the 75th percentile of the past decade — a level that has historically preceded RBI liquidity interventions and NBFC stress. The last time credit-deposit divergence was this acute (2022-23), RBI cut CRR by 50 bps and injected ₹2+ lakh cr via OMOs.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Across Sectors","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (prev 16.1%), capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (prev 75.6%) — both rising. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5% prior month, but still positive). Credit to industry at 19.5% YoY (19.2→20→18.2→19.5% over three months), agriculture credit at 19.5% YoY (16.8→17→17.2→19.5% rising three in a row). Vehicle credit at 18.8% YoY (15.2→18.8→19.7→18.8%). Iron ore prices at $161.91/t, up sharply from $90.86/t prior month.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Kirloskar, Escorts), cement (Ultratech, Ambuja), and steel (Tata Steel, JSW Steel). Capacity utilisation at 77.4% signals room for 3-5% more production before capex becomes urgent — but order books are filling. Allocate to project-linked infrastructure plays (L&T, Godrej & Boyce) and construction equipment rentals. Avoid consumer discretionary until capex cycle matures (12-18 months out).","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 68th percentile historically — a sweet spot that has preceded 18-24 month capex upcycles. The last time capex goods growth was this strong (2021-22), IIP capgoods sustained 15%+ growth for 8 consecutive quarters.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 94th Percentile Peak","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (latest), at the 94th percentile of the past decade — near all-time highs. signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Pause","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (prev 20.05%), at the 95th percentile of the past decade — a 3-year high. WPI at 9.92% YoY (prev 9.78%), rising. Food inflation at 8.94% YoY (3.47→5.52→7.74→8.94% rising three in a row). Brent crude at $89.9/bbl (flat), WTI at $82.79/bbl (flat), but FAO food index at 136 index (128.5→133.3→130.3→136, up 2 of last 3). CPI headline at 6.09% YoY (3.21→4.45→5.54→6.09% rising three in a row), core CPI at 4.5% YoY (3.4→3.9→4.5% rising 2 in a row).","implication":"RBI's rate pause is at risk if fuel and food inflation remain elevated. Reduce duration exposure in government securities — if CPI stays above 6% for another month, RBI will likely signal a rate hike in the next policy (April 2026). Hedge INR weakness — fuel inflation typically precedes INR depreciation as import bills rise. Avoid consumer staples with thin margins (HUL, ITC) until inflation moderates.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is at the 95th percentile — a level last seen in 2022 during the Russia-Ukraine shock. When fuel inflation exceeds 20% YoY, RBI has historically paused rate cuts and eventually raised rates within 2-3 months.","is_surprise":false}

(prev 1%), at 100th percentile — highest in the cycle, rising 2 in a row (0.75→1→1.25%). ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a. (prev 2.25%), rising 2 in a row (2→2.25→2.5%). signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down sharply from 14.1→15.08→14.1→15.08→19.5 mn sq ft over prior quarters — a 79% quarter-on-quarter collapse. Office vacancy at 13.4% vacant (14.37→14.8→14.37→14.8→13→13.4, down 3 of last 5), improving despite absorption collapse. Nifty IT index flat while office absorption craters. Bank Nifty at 63,063 index (60,792→61,519→61,034→61,787→62,273→62,039, up 3 of last 5) — financial services driving equity markets, not IT. Airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn / month (35.08→86.4→8.64, volatile but low). Rent in Bengaluru at ₹103.6/sqft/mo (109→163→103.6→168.8→168→103.6, volatile), Mumbai at ₹156/sqft/mo (178.7→156→135.8→342.6→343→156, volatile).","implication":"Traditional IT services are NOT the buyer of office space anymore — Global Capability Centers (GCCs) and captive operations are. GCCs are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses (hence lower absorption despite IT headcount growth). This decouples commercial real estate from IT stock performance. Overweight financial services (banks, NBFCs, insurance) and GCC-adjacent plays (Mindspace REIT, Embassy REIT) that cater to multinational captive operations. Underweight traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) on commercial real estate exposure — their office footprint is shrinking. The office market is bifurcating: premium Grade-A space for GCCs is tight; traditional IT space is oversupplied. Allocate to REITs with GCC-heavy portfolios.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter is at the 0th percentile — a structural break from the 14-19 mn sq ft / quarter norm of the past 5 years. This signals a permanent shift in how multinational corporations occupy space in India, not a cyclical downturn.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP Headline — Inflation Erodes the Foundation

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY, PMI Composite at 56.5, IIP Capital Goods at 16.9% YoY — three expansion signals aligned.
  • But CPI at 6.09% YoY has risen three consecutive months; core CPI at 4.5% YoY means this is no longer a food-spike story.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) and WPI at 9.92% YoY signal producer-price pass-through is underway.
  • FY estimate revised down to 7.1% YoY from 7.6%; core sector at 4.8% YoY, slipping even as capital goods surge.

The tension: Growth signals are genuine but inflation is now broad-based — food, fuel, and core all accelerating simultaneously. The RBI's pause was calibrated for a different inflation regime; at -84 bps real repo rate, policy is now inadvertently stimulative.

Bottom line: Watch core CPI: a third consecutive monthly rise above 4.5% YoY forces the RBI's hand regardless of growth optics.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

BOJ at Cycle Peak — Carry Unwind Finds EM Exits

The facts:

  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. — 100th percentile of the past decade, rising two in a row — is the most extreme central bank positioning globally.
  • Fed Funds at 3.88% p.a., rising three in a row; US 10Y Treasury at 5.07% yield (92nd percentile) — DM rates tightening in concert.
  • US GDP SAAR at 3.4%, rising three in a row; US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) — US re-acceleration is real, not survey noise.
  • But S&P 500 falling five in a row to 7,324; US VIX at 28.44, up four of last five — equity markets are not buying the growth story.

The tension: US macro data is accelerating while US equities are falling — the bond market at 5.07% yield is doing the tightening the Fed has not yet completed. BOJ at a 100th-percentile rate is the underappreciated catalyst: yen carry unwinds force EM selling regardless of India's domestic fundamentals.

Bottom line: BOJ's next move is the single biggest external risk to India flows; a further 25 bps hike would accelerate carry unwind and test INR at 94–95.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds — But FII Exit and CD Stress Tighten the Screws

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile) — domestic retail flows are structurally anchored despite market volatility.
  • But FII equity net at ₹-4,516 cr / month, negative; DII equity net at ₹6,222 cr / month, down sharply from ₹51,829 cr / month prior — DII absorption is fading.
  • DXY at 103.9, rising five in a row; INR at 93.46 ₹/USD (87th percentile) — dollar strength is structural, not episodic.
  • CD ratio at 82% credit ÷ deposits; bank credit at 19.54% YoY vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — system liquidity is being consumed faster than it is being created.

The tension: SIP inflows provide a floor, but DII net absorption has collapsed from ₹51,829 cr / month to ₹6,222 cr / month — the domestic institutional buffer is thinner than the SIP headline implies. FII outflows plus a weakening rupee plus a tightening CD ratio is a three-way liquidity squeeze.

Bottom line: If DII net equity absorption falls below ₹5,000 cr / month while FII remains negative, Nifty's 86th-percentile valuation has no domestic buyer of last resort.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at All-Time High; REITs Price the Office Collapse

The facts:

  • NRI residential buying is FALLING — NRI share at 18% of purchases (prior 15%, but down 2 pp vs earlier print); NRI share within premium/luxury at 32% — the segment most exposed to global carry and FX sentiment.
  • Premium ₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr band is oversupplied by 3 pp (34% of launches vs 31% of sales); Hyderabad leads with sales +15% YoY and launches +120% YoY — a supply surge that 28 months of unsold inventory cannot absorb.
  • Bank Nifty at 63,063 (100th percentile) — all-time high — while office absorption collapsed to 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter from 19.5 mn sq ft prior quarter.
  • Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down 12–30% from prior prints, pricing the absorption shock.

The tension: Bank Nifty at a 100th-percentile high is pricing credit growth and fee income; REIT prices are pricing an office demand collapse. Both cannot be right simultaneously — if GCC leasing has genuinely stalled, BFSI and IT services credit demand follows with a lag.

Bottom line: Avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 10 mn sq ft / quarter; Bank Nifty's all-time high is a short candidate if the CD ratio forces a risk-weight circular.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Inflation, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Inflation spiral: CPI at 6.09% YoY rising three in a row, core at 4.5% YoY, fuel at 22.93% YoY — if food inflation at 8.94% YoY does not reverse, RBI is forced to hike into a slowing FY estimate of 7.1% YoY.
  • BOJ carry unwind: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — every 25 bps hike accelerates yen repatriation, pressures INR at 93.46 ₹/USD (87th percentile), and forces FII selling beyond the current ₹-4,516 cr / month.
  • Credit-deposit crunch: CD ratio at 82% credit ÷ deposits with services credit at 28.3% YoY — RBI macro-prudential tightening via risk weights on unsecured lending is the most probable near-term policy action.
  • But Hyderabad office absorption at 4.2 mn sq ft / quarter (+92% YoY) and GCC occupier share at 42% suggest the national absorption collapse is a data anomaly, not a structural reversal — watch next quarter's print.

The tension: All three primary risks — inflation, carry unwind, credit tightening — are self-reinforcing: higher inflation delays cuts, higher BOJ rates pressure INR, INR weakness imports more inflation, and tighter credit slows the deposit mobilisation that could ease the CD ratio.

Bottom line: Watch November CPI (due ~12 Dec): a fourth consecutive monthly rise, or core above 4.8% YoY, ends the RBI pause narrative and reprices the entire rate curve.

"}
